sections.html:
Upson County sits in Georgia's west central region, about equally far from Atlanta, Macon and Columbus. Thomaston is the county seat. Housing ranges from mill-era homes in town to timber and farm tracts outside it. The county had an estimated 28,500 residents by mid-2025, a 2.9% gain since 2020. Owners occupy 61.0% of housing units, and a typical owner-held home is valued at $168,700.

The assessors manage more than 15,000 real property parcels and around 1,400 personal property accounts.

Both offices are at 305 South Hightower Street in Thomaston. Money owed goes to one door, and questions about value go to the other.

  • Tax commissioner, Suite D-120, (706) 647-8931, mailing to P.O. Box 409: billing, collection, tags and the payoff figure for a sale.
  • Tax assessors, Suite D-180, (706) 647-8176, mailing to P.O. Box 508, open weekdays through the working day: values, returns, exemptions and appeals.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, 116 W. Main Street: copies of your warranty deed.

The tax commissioner is an elected office that stands apart from both the assessors and the county commissioners. Statements are addressed to the homeowner and never to the lender, although the office sends mortgage companies a data file. After a change of lender, pass the bill along yourself.

The assessors arrive at fair market value, the whole 100% figure, and assessed value is 40% of that. Exemptions come off the 40%, which leaves the net assessed, or taxable, value. Multiply that by the millage rate to get the bill, with each mill worth one dollar on every $1,000.

Upson's rate is built from separate levies by the Board of Education, the county commissioners and the City of Thomaston, so the final rate on your statement depends on where the parcel sits. Property tax pays for county government and the public schools, public buildings, bridges and county roads, the courts, the jail and law enforcement, fire protection, and public health and sanitation.

Owners may also propose their own value by filing a return during the early-year window that ends April 1. If the assessors disagree, a notice goes out with their figure and the appeal clock starts.

sections.h2: When bills arrive and when they are due
sections.html:
Real and personal property bills are mailed no later than September 15, and the due date is around November 15. Mobile and manufactured home statements go out by January 30, and that tax comes due on April 1. If your bill rose from one year to the next, compare the rate on the statement with the prior year's, since the school board and the city set separate rates.

The post office's own date stamp proves a timely payment. A postage meter stamp does not.

Unpaid balances accrue monthly interest at the January prime rate plus 3%. After 120 days a 5% penalty is added, and another 5% joins it at each 120-day mark until penalties total 20%.

Hardship can justify partial payments, but only if you phone before the due date to arrange them, and interest and penalties keep running on the rest. The office sends a notice of intent with 30 days to pay before it files a FIFA lien on the General Execution Docket. Tax still unpaid 90 days past the due date is open to a lien, and credit bureaus can read those public records. Full payment, fees included, cancels the lien. Buying liens at the counter is not offered.

You have 45 days from the notice date. Four grounds qualify: taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption. Address the written appeal to the Board of Assessors and say which route you prefer.

The assessors also post a field review notice letting identified representatives walk onto a property in business hours to check its value, so do not be surprised by a visitor at the edge of your lot.

The county takes homestead applications from the first of the year through March 31, and they must reach the office by April 1. You must hold the house and live in it on January 1, and a stable owner needs no yearly renewal unless the deed or address changes. Ask at (706) 647-8176 which exemption amounts fit your parcel.

Have the tax commissioner write out a payoff before closing, and see that the closing agent pays it from what the buyer sends. Because the bill carries the name of whoever owned on New Year's Day, an autumn seller should check the settlement sheet to see who covers the current year.

Heirs and landlords should ask about every year they held the house, including any FIFA on file. A lien goes away only when it is paid in full, which is why the buyer's title agent will want the account clear.

A practical order of steps: ask the commissioner for the payoff, ask the assessors whether an exemption is attached to the parcel, order a deed copy from the Clerk of Superior Court if you cannot find yours, and give all three results to the closing agent. A cash purchase can settle old balances at closing and hand you the rest, which helps when a house carries back taxes, repairs or tenants.

faqs.q: How do I contact the Upson County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: The number is (706) 647-8931, and the counter is in Suite D-120 at 305 South Hightower Street, Thomaston.

faqs.q: When is Upson County property tax due?
faqs.a: Around November 15 in a typical year. Mobile and manufactured homes come due April 1.

faqs.q: What does late payment cost in Upson County?
faqs.a: Monthly interest equals prime plus 3%. A 5% penalty arrives at 120 days and returns at each 120-day mark, stopping at 20%.

faqs.q: What is the Upson County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice. Put it in writing for the Board of Assessors and name the appeal method.

faqs.q: Does Upson County mail my bill to my lender?
faqs.a: No. Statements go to the homeowner. Lenders get a data file, and passing the bill along is your job when needed.
